class.name: JarVoxelDebris
class.brief_description: Makes terrain that edits cut loose fall, and merges it back where it comes to rest.
class.description: Add it as a child of a [JarVoxelVolume]. After every edit, solid pieces of terrain no longer connected to the rest (at most [member max_size] voxels across) are cut out of the volume and become [JarVoxelDebrisBody] rigid bodies. They fall with the physics space's gravity (pointing at the [JarVoxelUniverse] anchor body when there are [JarCelestialBody] nodes) and collide with the terrain, characters and each other. A piece resting on the volume for [member merge_delay] seconds is merged back into it where it lies, with its materials, unless [member merge] is off. Detection runs on the volume's build thread after each edit and searches the edit's surroundings up to [member max_size] voxels away: a larger piece reaches past that and stays where it is. Pieces smaller than a few voxels are removed instead of falling. The pieces are shown as the terrain they came from (same material and shading, textures fixed to the piece). For networked games, turn [member merge] off and let the authority call [method merge_debris] when [signal debris_settled] fires. Nothing happens in the editor. Without this node the volume runs no debris code at all.

method.name: get_bodies
method.description: The pieces currently falling or resting, oldest first.

method.name: merge_debris
method.description: Puts [param body] back into the volume where it lies now (also when [member merge] is off). The body stops moving and is freed once the terrain shows it ([signal debris_merged]).

members.member: Physics layers of the pieces. 0 uses the volume's [member JarVoxelVolume.collision_layer]. Gravity areas (an [Area3D] with point gravity on a planet) only act on bodies in the layers their mask watches, so include one of those.
Physics layers the pieces collide with. 0 uses the volume's layer and mask (so they land on the terrain).
Mass of the pieces per cubic meter, in kg (rock is about 2500, soil about 1500).
Whether edits make pieces fall. Pieces already falling are not affected.
Most pieces at once; beyond this the oldest is merged back (or removed, with [member merge] off).

Largest piece that falls, in voxels across (on every axis). Larger loose pieces stay where they are. Also how far around each edit is searched: larger values cost more time per edit on the build thread.
Merge pieces back into the volume once they rest on it. Off: they stay rigid bodies (see [member max_bodies]).
Seconds a piece must rest before it merges (and before [signal debris_settled]).

signal.name: debris_detached
signal.description: A piece broke off and starts falling.

signal.name: debris_merged
signal.description: A piece is part of the terrain again; [param body] is freed right after.

signal.name: debris_settled
signal.description: A piece came to rest (for [member merge_delay] seconds).
